chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yahya, in what he knew, from Amr ibn Mudrik al-Ta'i, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions: 'Which bond of faith is the strongest?' So they said, 'Allah and His Rasool know best,' and some of them said, 'The Salat,' and some of them said, 'The Zakat,' and some of them said, 'The Sawm,' and some of them said, 'The Hajj and the Umrah,' and some of them said, 'The Jihad.' So Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For everything you said, there is merit, but that is not it. Rather, the strongest of the bonds of faith is love for Allah, and hatred for Allah, and the Wilayah of the Guardians of Allah, and the disavowal from the enemies of Allah.'

key_terms.التَّبَرِّي مِنْ أَعْدَاءِ اللَّهِ: Disavowal from the enemies of Allah
key_terms.تَوَالِي أَوْلِيَاءِ اللَّهِ: Allegiance to the friends of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the strongest bond of faith according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from Al-Kafi, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) elevates 'al-wala' wa al-barā' (allegiance and disavowal) as the strongest bond of faith, distinguishing the emotional core of belief from ritual obligations like prayer or fasting. This concept underpins the Shia doctrine of Tawhid al-Af'ali and Tawhid al-Sifat, linking theological monotheism directly to social and spiritual loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt and enmity toward their opponents. It establishes that true Iman is not merely performative but is defined by one's relational orientation toward the Divine and its representatives.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Al Hassan Ali in Yahya among what he knew from Amro Bin Mudrak Al Taiy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww said to hissaww companions: ‘Which bond of the Emān is the strongest?’ So they said, ‘Allahazwj and Hisazwj Rasoolsaww are more knowing’, and some of them said, ‘The Salāt’, and some of them said, ‘The Zakāt’, and some of them said, ‘The Fasts’, and some of them said, ‘The Hajj and the Umrah’, and some of them said, ‘The Jihād’. So Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘For everything what you said, there is a merit, and that is not it, but the strongest of the bonds of the Emān is the love regarding Allahazwj, and the hatred regarding Allahazwj, and the Wilayah of the Guardiansasws of Allahazwj, and the disavowing from the enemies of Allahazwj’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from abu al-Hassan Ali ibn Yahya (as far as I know) from ‘Amr ibn Mudrik al-Ta’i from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah once asked his companions, ‘Which ring of belief is stronger to hold on to?’ They said, ‘Allah and His Messenger know best.’ Certain individuals among them said, ‘It is prayer,’ others said, ‘It is al-Zakat (charity)’, a few of them said, ‘It is fasting’, others said, ‘It is Hajj and ‘Umrah’ and still others said, ‘It is Jihad (hard work against the enemies).’ “The Messenger of Allah then said, ‘For everything you said there is a merit but is not such a ring. In fact the strongest ring of belief to hold on to is love for the sake of Allah, hate for the sake of Allah, support and love those who have received authority from Allah and to disassociate from the enemies of Allah.’”
